question.problem:
Consider the equivalence relation $∼$ on $Z,$ defined by $x∼y$ if $2\,|\,(x-y).$ Which of the following equivalence classes contain the element $9?$

I. $[5]$

II. $[2]$

III. $[19]$
question.worked_solution:
We have $9\in [x]$ if $9∼x.$ Using the definition of the given equivalence relation, we require

$$
\begin{aligned}2\,|\,(9-x).\end{aligned}
$$

Let's now consider each of the given equivalence classes.

- $9\in [5]$ because $2\,|\,(9-5)\,✓$

- $9\notin [2]$ because $2∤(9-2)\,\times $

- $9\in [19]$ because $2\,|\,(9-19)\,✓$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only".
